questions.stem: The extracellular concentration of a positive ion (with valency1) is 10 mmol/L and its intracellular concentration is 10 mmol/L, the potential across the membrane using the Nernst equation is (mV):
questions.solutionHtml:
60
  • The potential across the membrane using the Nernst equation is +60mV.
  • EMF (millivolts) = 1/z 61x log Concentration on one side/Concentration on another side.
  • Where Z is valency.
  • Deriving the numerical value:
  • EMF=61*log 100/10
  • =61*log10.
  • =61*1 (since log 10 =1)
  • =61mV
  • Deciding the charge: The higher potassium concentration in the extracellular fluid means the potassium ions diffuse into the cell. To prevent this, a positive potential is required inside the cell.
  • Hence, the potential across the membrane using the Nernst equation is +60mV.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 9

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman collapsed due to an anxiety attack. The Emergency Medical Team who arrives on the scene notes that she is hyperventilating and suspects that she is suffering from tetany, a continuous contraction of skeletal muscle fibers caused by an increase in the excitability of nerves and muscle membranes. The increased membrane excitability is caused by which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased release of inhibitory neurotransmitters from nerve terminals

options.label: B
options.text: Depolarization of the nerve and muscle membranes

options.label: C
options.text: Spontaneous release of calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum

options.label: D
options.text: Activation of sodium channels at more negative membrane potentials

questions.answerText: Depolarization of the nerve and muscle membranes
questions.solutionHtml:
Depolarization of the nerve and muscle membranes

Membrane excitability is related to the ease with which depolarization opens   channels.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 59, 382, 692

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman undergoing surgery for appendicitis develops malignant hyperthermia following halothane anesthesia. The life-threatening increase in metabolic rate and body temperature is attributed to a mutation of the ryanodine receptor in skeletal muscle, resulting in which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Excess calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) during muscle contraction.

options.label: B
options.text: The rapid repetitive firing of the presynaptic terminals of motor neurons.

options.label: C
options.text: The inability of skeletal muscle cells to repolarize.

options.label: D
options.text: An increase in the refractory period of the motor neurons.

questions.answerText: Excess calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) during muscle contraction.
questions.solutionHtml:
Excess calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) during muscle contraction.

Malignant Hyperthermia is associated with a genetic defect in the RyR1Q calcium channel of the skeletal muscle sarcoplasmic reticulum that permits uncontrolled calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum when precipitating drugs are given.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 255

questions.stemHtml: At which point on the action potential shown in the diagram below is the membrane closest to the Na+ equilibrium potential?
questions.solutionHtml:
Point A
  • The Na+ equilibrium potential is approximately +60 mV and is based on the ratio of the intracellular and extracellular Na+ concentrations.
  • During an action potential, the peak of the action potential (point A) is close, but not equal, to the Na+ equilibrium potential.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 7–8.

questions.stem: Suppose a resting myocardial cell membrane is altered to be relatively more permeable to sodium than to potassium, then the resting membrane potential would be nearest to which of the following values?
questions.solutionHtml:
+60 mV
  • If a cell membrane is relatively permeable to one ion and impermeable to other ions, then the resting membrane potential of the cell will be near the equilibrium potential for the ion that it is more permeable.
  • In this case, the membrane is most permeable to sodium, so the resting membrane potential will be closest to the sodium equilibrium potential, which is +60 mV.
  • So, the correct answer is C and the rest of the other options are false.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, Edition 14th, Page No. 63

questions.stem: The true statement regarding the action potential in a nerve is:

options.label: A
options.text: Depolarization is a result of the outward movement of potassium ions.

options.label: B
options.text: The action potential occurs due to the sudden opening of Na+ channels.

options.label: C
options.text: The action potential occurs when the potential reaches a threshold at -75 mV.

options.label: D
options.text: The resting membrane potential is -95 mV.

questions.answerText: The action potential occurs due to the sudden opening of Na+ channels.
questions.solutionHtml:
The action potential occurs due to the sudden opening of Na+ channels.

The action potential occurs due to the sudden opening of Na+ channels- at the onset of the action potential, the sodium channels instantaneously become activated and allow up to a 5000-fold increase in sodium conductance.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, Edition 14th, Page No. 63-65.

options.label: A
options.text: Effect of one non-diffusible ion on the distribution of another non-diffusible ion.

options.label: B
options.text: Effect of one permeant ion on the distribution of another permeant ion.

options.label: C
options.text: Effect of a permeant ion on the distribution of non-diffusible ions.

options.label: D
options.text: Effect of a non-diffusible ion on the distribution of permeant ions.

questions.answerText: Effect of a non-diffusible ion on the distribution of permeant ions.
questions.solutionHtml:
Effect of a non-diffusible ion on the distribution of permeant ions.

Gibbs Donnan equilibrium explains the effect of non-diffusible ions on the distribution of permeant ions.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 08.

questions.stem: Which of the following would cause an immediate reduction in the amount of potassium leaking out of a cell?

options.label: A
options.text: Increasing the permeability of the membrane to potassium

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing the activity of the sodium-potassium pump

questions.solutionHtml:
Hyperpolarizing the membrane potential

Hyperpolarizing the membrane makes the inside of the cell more negative and therefore, makes it more difficult for potassium to flow out of the cell.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 7–8

questions.stem: End plate potential follows which law?
questions.solutionHtml:
All or none law

The events occurring during the transmission of impulses from the motor nerve to the muscle are somewhat similar to those occurring at neuron-to-neuron synapses.

The End Plate Potential (EPP) follows the All or None Law.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 124.

questions.stem: The resting transmembrane potential (Vm ) of a nerve axon is essential for signal generation. Instantaneous elimination of which of the following would most rapidly bring Vm close to 0 mV?

options.label: A
options.text: Active transport of K+ out of the cell

options.label: B
options.text: Active transport of Na+ out of the cell

questions.solutionHtml:
High membrane permeability to K+
  • The immediate cause of the resting potential is the high membrane permeability to K+ compared with other ions; if this permeability were to be eliminated, Vm would instantly depolarize to within several mV of 0 mV. It would not quite reach 0 mV because of the electrogenic effect of the Na+-K+-ATPase (which pumps three Na+ ions out for every two K+ ions pumped in).


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 124.

questions.stem: Hyperkalemia reduces the excitability of neurons and muscle cells. Which of the following best describes the effect of increased extracellular potassium [K+]?

options.label: A
options.text: Depolarizes the cell, thus reducing action potential amplitude.

options.label: B
options.text: Depolarizes the cell, thus inactivating voltage-gated Na+ channels.

options.label: C
options.text: Hyperpolarizes the cell, which increases the action potential threshold.

options.label: D
options.text: Increases the activity of the Na-K-ATPase, which hyperpolarizes the cell.

questions.answerText: Depolarizes the cell, thus inactivating voltage-gated Na+ channels.
questions.solutionHtml:
Depolarizes the cell, thus inactivating voltage-gated Na+ channels.

Sustained depolarization, as occurs with hyperkalemia, inactivates voltage-gated Na+ channels, which remain inactivated until the membrane repolarizes, thus blocking action potential generation.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 124 & 127.

Axon
Antidromic conduction is seen in Axon.

An antidromic impulse in an axon refers to conduction opposite of the normal (orthodromic) direction.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 88.

questions.stem: The permeability to which of the following ions increases during the depolarization of a nerve fiber:
questions.solutionHtml:
Na+

The ion permeability that increases during the depolarization of a nerve fiber is primarily the permeability to sodium ions (Na+).

 

  • Depolarization Stage. At this time, the membrane suddenly becomes permeable to sodium ions, allowing tremendous numbers of positively charged sodium ions to diffuse to the interior of the axon.
  • The normal “polarized” state of −90 millivolts is immediately neutralized by the inflowing positively charged sodium ions, with the potential rising rapidly in the positive direction—a process called depolarization.
  • In large nerve fibers, the great excess of positive Na+ moving to the inside causes the membrane potential to actually “overshoot”.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page Number: 65.

questions.stem: The resting membrane potential of the nerve is determined by the concentration of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Potassium

The resting membrane potential of a nerve is primarily determined by the concentration gradient of potassium ions (K+) inside and outside the cell.

  • In neurons, the concentration of K+ is much higher inside than outside the cell, while the reverse is the case for Na+.
  • The outward K+ concentration gradient results in the passive movement of K+ out of the cell when K+ -selective channels are open.
  • Similarly, the inward Na+ concentration gradient results in the passive movement of Na+ into the cell when Na+-selective channels are open.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 84-85

questions.stem: Due to the activation of ion channels of the external membrane of the excitable cell, its rest potential has significantly increased. What channels were activated?
questions.solutionHtml:
Potassium channels
The activation of ion channels on the external membrane of an excitable cell that results in a significant increase in the resting potential is most likely due to the opening of potassium (K+) channels.
  • A negative overshoot called hyperpolarization occurs when potassium gates stay open longer than Na gates, so the amount of potassium that leaves the cell is greater than the amount of sodium that entered.
  • Therefore, the membrane voltage drops to 1 or 2 mV more negatively than the original RMP (when RMP becomes more negative, it means that RMP increased).

 

Therefore, the most likely scenario for a significant increase in the resting membrane potential is the activation of potassium channels.

 




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 84-85., Costanzo Physiology 6th Edition Page Number 18.
